evidence.supportingExcerpt: Ohlund and colleagues described alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-high myofibroblastic fibroblasts near pancreatic cancer cells and IL-6-producing inflammatory populations farther away in pancreatic models and samples. This is not an exhaustive classification of breast stroma or a permanent job assignment for each cell. Ozdemir reported that depletion of selected alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive myofibroblasts worsened disease and immunosuppression in pancreatic mouse models. Removing all fibroblasts is not a general treatment conclusion. The indexed 2015 correction is linked; its body was unavailable for this review, so no correction-specific figure claim is adopted.

remaining: The indexed 2019 Garcia-Diaz correction resolves to DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.11.113, but its body is inaccessible. The primary abstract and reader passage support the named axis at their recorded scope; correction-specific implications are not certified.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Scope Garcia-Diaz’s JAK1/JAK2–STAT1/2/3–IRF1 mechanism to melanoma experiments; verify rather than repeat a mainly-STAT1 simplification.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.

point.requirement: FGFR2 fusions join the receptor's kinase to a partner that forces it on. In a phase 2 study of pemigatinib, an FGFR inhibitor, 38 of 107 people (35.5%) with cholangiocarcinoma carrying such fusions had tumor shrinkage [5]. The fusion drives the very kinase the drug blocks.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The original FIGHT-202 report observed responses in 38 of 107 people, 35.5 per cent, with previously treated cholangiocarcinoma and qualifying FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements given pemigatinib. The denominator includes fusions or rearrangements, not only one fusion mechanism. A 2024 correction is linked to the report; its text was unavailable, so the figure here is from the original abstract rather than a correction-checked final estimate. It is a named single-arm clinical signal rather than evidence for any receptor variant or another disease. For an uncharacterised receptor variant, compare with the normal receptor at matched expression and measure appropriate phosphorylation and downstream changes. Similar amount without extra activation does not support activation in that condition, while leaving other conditions unresolved. An activating receptor fusion or amplification may still require its kinase, whereas an active downstream RAS route can bypass the proposed receptor step. Locate the drug's blocked step and possible downstream bypass, then separately test whether changing the output matters for growth. Neither a bulk ligand signal from a sender nor receptor presence assigns an active signal to the malignant receiver.
